opening_message:
Ticket 1: Haley Roberts (employee ID E021) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E021.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Haley Roberts (E021) is a full-time Engineer requesting write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; request is at the allowed level. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E021 (Haley Roberts) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training limits max to read. Requested write exceeds maximum; recommend read.
reason: The two agent notes conflict on Haley Roberts' employment type: HR states full_time (recommending write), while Security states contractor with basic security training (recommending read). Under the access policy, a contractor with only basic training may have at most read access; requested write exceeds that maximum, so the maximum (read) should be granted. Given the conflicting evidence, I grant the more restrictive allowed level (read), which complies with policy under the Security database's information.
